title: LoginComplete is sent the moment PlayerTeleport/PlayerCreate arrives; retail sends it after the tunnel's world fade-in, so ACE drops the teleport/login invulnerability while the player still sees portal space
decomp_evidence: gmSmartBoxUI::UseTime (acclient.c:262368): the TAS 6 WORLD_FADEIN exit at :262566-262571 is `CPlayerSystem::SendLoginCompleteNotification(v3); CPlayerSystem::SetTeleportInProgress(v3, 0);`. With no animation running, it sends only once `SmartBox::teleport_occured` (:262578-262580). SendLoginCompleteNotification (:400381) additionally gates on `ACCWeenieObject::AllContainedObjectsExist` and otherwise sets sendLoginCompletePending. teleport_in_progress (:143092) is `player && !position_update_complete`, and SmartBox::UseTime (:146256) sets position_update_complete only when `!cell_manager->blocking_for_cells && !waiting_for_teleport` (:146268-146282). So the send comes after cells are loaded + >=2 s CONTINUE + 1 s fade-out + 1 s fade-in.
openac_evidence: TeleportAnimSequencer.cs:23 `FireLoginComplete, // WorldFadeIn -> Off: send GameAction 0xA1` (emitted at :136-140). LocalPlayerTeleportController.cs:911-915 handles it with `_session.SendLoginComplete()`, and the login presentation does the same at :1225-1229.
holt_evidence: src/session/messages/position.rs:179 `if holtburger_core::client::DEFER_LOGIN_COMPLETE_AFTER_TELEPORT {` (const is `false`, holtburger-core client/mod.rs:90). The else-arm sends `GameAction::LoginComplete` immediately in the PlayerTeleport arm. When the const is on it only defers to the first self UpdatePosition (position.rs:264), which ACE emits right after PlayerTeleport, so it is still seconds before the tunnel ends. Login: src/session/messages/login.rs:193 sends LoginComplete on PlayerCreate. portal_space.js header: 'NOT PORTED: LoginComplete timing'. The portal 'done' event (portal_space.js:668) sends nothing.
discrepancy: ACE keeps a teleporting/logging-in player Teleporting+Hidden until LoginComplete (Player_Location.cs:740-761 OnTeleportComplete; Player_Networking.cs:25). While Teleporting, monsters skip them (Monster_Awareness.cs:353), attacks are refused (Player_Combat.cs:906 `!target.Teleporting`) and AutonomousPosition is dropped (Player_Tick.cs:417). Holtburger clears this protection at once. On a portal hop the player can be aggroed and hit for the 4-8 s the tunnel is up. On a slow-link cold login (minutes to a playable world) they stand materialized in the world while the client is still loading.
proposed_change: 1) Add a wasm export `sendLoginComplete()` (SessionHandle, a typeof-guarded JS call) that sends GameAction::LoginComplete. 2) Behind `?retailLoginComplete` (default ON, =off restores today's immediate send), stop the immediate sends in position.rs (PlayerTeleport arm) and login.rs (PlayerCreate arm). Instead: (a) portal_space.js calls `sessionHandle.sendLoginComplete()` on the 'done' event (end of WORLD_FADEIN), on the TUNNEL_HOLD_MAX/cells-wait failsafe exits, and in endPortalSpace when it is torn down early; (b) client_events.js calls it directly on TeleportArrived (kind 66) when `?portalSpace=off` or startPortalSpace did not run; (c) login: call it when the boot gate reaches in-world-ready (spawn LB resident), or immediately when there is no renderer (headless/nullRender bots). 3) Add a wasm-side safety net: if JS hasn't asked within ~25 s of PlayerTeleport/PlayerCreate, send anyway. ACE logs a teleporting player off after 5 min (Player_Tick.cs:107,135). 4) Retire the DEFER_LOGIN_COMPLETE_AFTER_TELEPORT const (its deferral point is the wrong edge).
test_plan: Node: extend test_portal_space_sequencer.mjs with a fake sessionHandle and assert sendLoginComplete is called exactly once per teleport: on 'done', on each failsafe exit, and on the portalSpace=off arrival path. Rust: a holtburger-web lib test that the PlayerTeleport arm does not send LoginComplete when the gate is on and that the timeout net fires. Live (orchestrator): @telepoi into a monster area. The server log should show OnTeleportComplete after the tunnel, not at PlayerTeleport, and no damage taken while the tunnel is up. Also check that movement right after the fade-in is accepted (no rubber-band).
already_tracked: Partly. holtburger-core DEFER_LOGIN_COMPLETE_AFTER_TELEPORT (default off, defers only to the first UpdatePosition) and the portal_space.js 'NOT PORTED: LoginComplete timing' note. Not in the round-1/2 ledgers.

title: The retail teleport hook never runs for the local player: autorun (and any local MoveTo) survives a portal, and CommandInterpreter::PlayerTeleported is dead code
decomp_evidence: SmartBox::PlayerPositionUpdated(teleporting=1) (acclient.c:144695-144712) runs `CPhysicsObj::teleport_hook(v5, 1)` and then a cmdinterp virtual. TeleportPlayer (:144733-144744) calls it with teleporting=1. teleport_hook (:322237) runs MovementManager::CancelMoveTo(0x3C = WeenieError ITeleported), PositionManager::UnStick/StopInterpolating/UnConstrain, then TargetManager::ClearTarget + NotifyVoyeurOfEvent(Teleported_TargetStatus) and report_collision_end. CommandInterpreter::PlayerTeleported (:716924-716931) runs SetAutoRun(0,1) (vfptr[17]) and then SendMovementEvent. CAVEAT for the verifier: I did not resolve the vtable slot `cmdinterp->vfptr[9].OnLoseFocus` (IInputActionCallbackVtbl has 3 entries per index, so this is slot 29) to PlayerTeleported. The mapping is inferred: the holtburger staged port and OpenAC's 'PlayerTeleported port' both treat it that way. teleport_hook's CancelMoveTo/UnStick/ClearTarget part is directly verified.
openac_evidence: RuntimeAcceptedPositionDriveController.cs:433 `bool autorunCancelled = _localMovementState()?.CancelAutoRun() ?? false;` followed by `_localPlayerOutbound.TrySendMovement(...)` on the portal arrival commit (ReconcileAndAcknowledgePortal). The test at RuntimeAcceptedPositionDriveControllerTests.cs:1547 names it 'the portal arm's PlayerTeleported port'.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-core/src/client/movement/command_interpreter.rs:795-801 `PlayerTeleported` is `#[allow(dead_code)] // staged: teleport wiring`. MovementSystem::set_auto_run (system.rs:3644-3660) is the only writer of `auto_run`. The teleport arms (position.rs PlayerTeleport; core messages.rs:489-524) only run `handle_exit_world_for` (the motion-queue drain, system.rs:9102-9109) and suspend bodies. Autorun is live by default: `?retailRunKeys` reads `!== "off"` (scene3d/input.js readRetailRunKeysFlag). index.html:5342-5343 keeps a JS mirror `window.__autoRunOn` that nothing clears.
discrepancy: A player who portals while autorunning arrives still running and runs off from the drop point, often straight off the arrival pad. Retail and OpenAC stop autorun and send a fresh movement event. Any local pursuit (use-at-range walk) is not cancelled with ITeleported either.
proposed_change: On the local teleport (wasm PlayerTeleport arm, and/or the destination UpdatePosition that fires TeleportArrived), call a new MovementSystem::player_teleported(). It runs set_auto_run(false), cancels any pending S10 pursuit (PendingPursuitCommand::Cancel{restore_manual:false}, the CancelMoveTo(ITeleported) analogue) and requests a MoveToState send. Wire the staged CommandInterpreter::player_teleported where the interp lane is active. In JS, clear `window.__autoRunOn` on PORTAL_SPACE_ENTERED (client_events.js). Escape: `?teleportHook=off`.
test_plan: Rust (core): with set_auto_run(true), a PlayerTeleport-driven player_teleported() leaves auto_run false, emits one MoveToState, and drops a pending pursuit. Node: client_events kind=33 clears window.__autoRunOn. Live: toggle autorun (R), use a portal, and confirm the character stands at the destination.

title: Portal-space reveal waits only for the destination LB's terrain mesh (outdoor) or one cell container (indoor), then force-reveals 6 s after arrival; retail blocks until the whole prefetch window is loaded
decomp_evidence: CellManager::ChangePosition (acclient.c:146646) with blocking=teleporting calls PreFetchCells (:146528). Outdoors that is LScape::PreFetchCells (:307068), which walks the whole `mid_radius` window and per LB prefetches the block, its LandBlockInfo and `CLandBlock::PreFetchCells`. Indoors it is CEnvCell::PreFetchCells (:348023): the LB, its info, every one of `num_cells` EnvCells, and the LScape window when `seen_outside`. Any miss leaves blocking_for_cells set. SmartBox::UseTime (:146268-146270) then does nothing but CheckPrefetchStatus, with no physics or object maintenance, and teleport_in_progress stays true. There is no timeout.
openac_evidence: WorldRevealReadinessBarrier.Evaluate (WorldRevealReadinessBarrier.cs) requires render neighbourhood (near/far radius) && composite textures && collision. Collision is the spawn cell indoors or the terrain neighbourhood at far radius outdoors, plus `!_hasLiveCollisionPendingRestore`. There is no cap; a wait cue is shown instead (RuntimeWorldTransitState.ObserveWait).
holt_evidence: scene3d/portal_space.js:229-238 destinationCellsReady: indoor checks `cellContainers3d.has(id)`, outdoor checks `terrainBakedLbs.has(lb)`. Statics, buildings, neighbouring LBs and the wasm collision bakes (app/landblock_stream.js terrainPrefetchedLbs / buildingAabbsPopulatedLbs / cellContainersPopulatedLbs) are not consulted. :89 `ARRIVAL_CELLS_WAIT_MAX = 6.0` and :647 reveal anyway.
discrepancy: On an outdoor arrival the tunnel can lift onto bare terrain: town buildings, statics and the neighbouring LBs pop in afterwards, and building collision may not exist yet. On any slow link the 6 s cap reveals an unstreamed world, which retail never does.
proposed_change: Widen destinationCellsReady. Outdoors: terrainBakedLbs for the destination LB and its in-range Chebyshev-1 neighbours, plus buildingsBakedLbs and staticsBakedLbs for the destination LB. Indoors: the cell container plus envCellLoadedLbs for the LB, plus the outdoor rule when `isCellSeenOutside(cell)`. Both: the wasm collision bake for the destination LB (publish landblock_stream's cellContainersPopulatedLbs/buildingAabbsPopulatedLbs on scene3d or pass an accessor). Raise ARRIVAL_CELLS_WAIT_MAX from 6 s to ~20 s and keep the 'In Portal Space - Please Wait...' notice up. Escape `?revealGate=thin` restores today's predicate. Check that a bake of an empty LB (no buildings/statics) still adds to the Baked sets, so the gate cannot stall.
test_plan: Node: unit-test destinationCellsReady with fake scene3d Sets (outdoor needs the dest + neighbours + buildings/statics; indoor seen-outside needs the outdoor half) and the 20 s cap path in the existing portal sequencer test. Live 1070 eye-test: Holtburg <-> Rithwic @telepoi. The tunnel should lift onto a populated town, a little later than today.
already_tracked: No. PARITY-STATUS portal_space_teleport lists only owner retests.

title: The indoor stream gates treat seen-outside building interiors like sealed dungeons: arriving inside a town building streams only a 3x3 ring and admits no outdoor loaders until the first outdoor packet
decomp_evidence: CellManager::ChangePosition (acclient.c:146646): for an EnvCell, only `!seen_outside && !keep_lscape_loaded` calls LScape::release_all (:146700-146703). A seen_outside cell takes `v13 = Position::get_outside_cell_id(p); LScape::update_loadpoint(v6->lscape, v13);` (:146754-146755), so the full landscape window keeps following the building. CEnvCell::PreFetchCells (:348023) also prefetches the LScape window when `seen_outside`.
openac_evidence: DungeonStreamingGate.Compute(isTeleportHold, currCellIsSealedDungeon, currCellId) collapses streaming only for a sealed dungeon (SealedDungeonCellClassifier), not for every EnvCell.
holt_evidence: scene3d/world_stream.js:162 isIndoorCell is `(landblockId & 0xffff) >= 0x100`, and :270 `const gateHeld = indoors && DUNGEON_STREAM_GATE_ON;` holds the terrain ring + buildings/statics/spawns loaders for every EnvCell. scene3d/cells.js:3589 `if (indoor) ringRadius = INDOOR_PVS_RING_RADIUS;` (default 1, :853-863) for every indoor cell. The comment justifies it as 'a dungeon/interior can't see the surface LBs', which is untrue for doorways and windows. The wasm already exports isCurrentCellSeenOutside / isCellSeenOutside (src/lib.rs:38234, :38312).
discrepancy: Logging in, recalling or portalling into a town building (meeting halls, shops, mansions) gets a 1-LB horizon through the door and windows, and a whole-ring cold bake on the first step outside. Retail keeps the normal landscape window around a seen-outside interior. (Walking in from outside is mostly fine, because LRU eviction is pressure-driven.)
proposed_change: Key both gates on 'indoor AND NOT seen_outside' (retail's release_all condition). In world_stream.js, hold only when `isCellSeenOutside(upd.landblockId)` is false; an unknown/non-resident cell stays held, as today. In cells.js, collapse the ring only when `isCurrentCellIndoor() && !isCurrentCellSeenOutside()`. The sealed purge (_sealedEvictLbKey) is unchanged. Flag `?seenOutsideRing` (default on, =off escape).
test_plan: Node: test_a15_q4_renderer_neutral_core.mjs-style harness for world_stream with a fake session whose isCellSeenOutside returns true: assert ringEvals increments for an indoor packet. A cells.js ring-radius unit with stubbed isCurrentCellSeenOutside. Live: log in inside the Holtburg meeting hall and check the horizon through the door matches standing outside. Watch resident LB count and frame time inside buildings.

title: No 'teleport in progress' gating: retail raises the UI busy count for the whole portal sequence and refuses combat-mode changes in portal space
decomp_evidence: CPlayerSystem::SetTeleportInProgress (acclient.c:395704-395723) calls ClientUISystem::IncrementBusyCount on true and DecrementBusyCount on false. gmSmartBoxUI::UseTime sets it true on TAS_TUNNEL (:262424) and false after LoginComplete (:262571). ClientCombatSystem::SetCombatMode (0x56BE30, :408787) refuses with `"You can't enter combat mode while in portal space"` when `CPlayerSystem::GetPlayerSystem()->teleportInProgress` (:408840-408845).
openac_evidence: LocalPlayerTeleportController ends mouse-look and gates input across the transit (`_input.EndMouseLook()` at :581/:704; ILocalPlayerTeleportInputLifetime).
holt_evidence: No portal-space check in any combat-mode or use path: a search for "while in portal space" returns nothing. The toggle key calls `handle.toggleCombatMode()` directly (index.html:5437). portal_space.js exports isPortalSpaceActive() (:614) but only scene3d/index.js uses portalSpaceOwnsFrame() for rendering.
discrepancy: During the tunnel a player can toggle combat stance, use or drag items and start casts against a world they cannot see. Retail blocks these locally with the busy count and prints the combat-mode refusal.
proposed_change: While isPortalSpaceActive(): (a) refuse the combat-mode toggle (index.html key path + plugins/api.js toggleCombatMode) with retail text in chat channel 0x1A; (b) treat portal space as busy in the existing local busy gates (item use/drag, cast pre-check), i.e. the same refusal as a busy count > 0. Flag `?portalBusy` (default on).
test_plan: Node: a stubbed portal-space active state makes toggleCombatMode emit the refusal line and send nothing. Live: press the combat key in the tunnel.

title: Retail's open-sea wall (an all-water landblock blocks non-viewer, non-missile movers) never fires: the faithful outdoor cell's block water type is always NotWater
decomp_evidence: CLandCell find_env_collisions body (acclient.c:354995-355058): after find_terrain_poly, `if ( CObjCell::get_block_water_type(...) == 2 && !(v2->object_info.state & 4) && !(v2->object_info.object->state & 0x40) ) return 2;` (Collided unless IS_VIEWER or PhysicsState MISSILE). CObjCell::get_block_water_type (:346439) returns myLandBlock_->water_type. CLandBlockStruct::CalcWater (:354566) sets the block water_type to 2 only when every one of the 8x8 cells is all-water (CalcCellWater :353608 with TERRAIN_SURF_CHAR :41303, WATER = codes 16-20). An entirely-water CELL inside a partly-water block is not a wall: get_water_depth (:347233) returns 0.9 and validate_walkable (:314161) lets the sphere sink that far.
openac_evidence: TerrainSurface.cs computes `BlockWaterType` ('Only a full 8 x 8 block can be sea'; `IsEntirelyWater => BlockWaterType == 2`). tests/AcDream.Core.Tests/Physics/OpenSeaBarrierTests.cs: Player_CannotWalkOntoTheOpenSea, CameraAndMissiles_CrossTheOpenSea, Player_CanWadeWhereTheBlockIsOnlyPartlyWater.
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/faithful_bridge.rs:313 `if self.get_block_water_type() == WaterType::EntirelyWater && ... IS_VIEWER == 0 { return Collided }`. It uses the trait default (crates/holtburger-dat/src/transition/objcell.rs:243-249: `match self.cur_landblock() { Some(lb) => lb.water_type(), None => NotWater }`), and SceneObjCell::cur_landblock is `None` (faithful_bridge.rs:438-440). The code's own comment (:310-311) says it 'never fires until live water is wired (WS8)'. The MISSILE exemption is also missing ('Missile is not a movement mover on this path'), but projectiles now sweep CTransition (round-1 physupd-1). url-flags.md's faithfulOutdoor row claims the player 'can't walk into deep water'.
discrepancy: With the default ?faithfulOutdoor path a player can walk off the coast onto open ocean landblocks: sunk 0.9 m but otherwise free. ACE takes client positions, so this reaches the server. Retail stops them at the edge of the first all-water landblock.
proposed_change: Compute the landblock water type once per LB from the 81 codes already returned by `scene.terrain_cell_water_codes` (block = 2 iff all 64 cells are EntirelyWater, i.e. all 81 vertices water; 1 if any water; else 0). Carry it on SceneObjCell (new `block_water_type` field set in build_outdoor_cell) and override get_block_water_type to return it. In find_terrain_collisions add the retail MISSILE exemption: `&& transition.object_info.object.state & PhysicsState::MISSILE == 0`. Escape `?openSeaWall=off` (default on).
test_plan: holtburger-world faithful_bridge tests mirroring OpenAC OpenSeaBarrierTests: an all-water LB refuses a grounded player step (pose unchanged); IS_VIEWER and a MISSILE-state body pass; a block with one dry vertex lets the player wade (entirely-water cell gets depth 0.9 and is not a wall). Live: walk to the coast south of Holtburg; the player should stop at the open-sea boundary.

title: Housing barriers are never enforced: cell restriction objects (EnvCell restriction_obj and the outdoor LandBlockInfo RestrictionTables) are parsed but the live cell reports restriction_obj = 0
decomp_evidence: CObjCell::check_entry_restrictions (acclient.c:347102-347137): for a mover with a weenie and `object_info.state & 0x100` (IS_PLAYER), if `restriction_obj` is set and the mover cannot bypass (weenie vfptr[18]), it looks up the restriction object. A missing object, or `vfptr[17](mover)` (CanMoveInto) false, gives handle_move_restriction + return 2 (Collided). The land-cell collision body calls it first (:355019). Outdoor cells get their restriction id from the LandBlockInfo table: CLandBlockInfo::GetRestrictionIID (:351250), assigned per lcell at :352878-352880. CLandCell::handle_move_restriction (:355063) sets an axis-aligned collision normal.
openac_evidence: TransitionTypes.cs:103-125 ObjectInfo.CheckEntryRestrictions: players only; CanBypassMoveRestrictions; restriction object missing => Collided; house owner == mover => OK; otherwise `restrictions.IsAllowedIn(moverId, moverMonarchId)`. Called at TransitionTypes.cs:2360 with `cellPhysics?.RestrictionObj` (PhysicsDataCache.cs:479/631 copies EnvCell.RestrictionObj). ACE ObjCell.cs:286-325 has the same check, with the comment 'acclient checks for entry restrictions (housing barriers)'.
holt_evidence: The seam is ported (crates/holtburger-dat/src/transition/objcell.rs:320-322 `if self.restriction_obj() != 0 && !can_bypass {`), but the live bridge returns 0 for every cell: crates/holtburger-world/src/spatial/faithful_bridge.rs:442-444 `fn restriction_obj(&self) -> u32 { 0 }`. The data exists but is unused: EnvCell `restriction_obj` (holtburger-dat file_type/env_cell.rs:255,298-300), LandBlockInfo `restriction_tables` (holtburger-dat landblock.rs:176,190), the house weenie's HouseRestrictions (holtburger-protocol object description.rs:26,192) and house_owner (holtburger-world hydration.rs:158).
discrepancy: Holtburger players walk straight into other players' houses and walled yards (mansion/villa plots). Retail bounces them off the barrier. ACE's server physics only runs the check on its own transitions, so the client is where retail enforces it.
proposed_change: 1) In SpatialScene, store the restriction id per cell: EnvCell restriction_obj when the env cell is ingested, and the LandBlockInfo RestrictionTables mapping (landcell id -> house guid) for outdoor cells. 2) SceneObjCell::restriction_obj returns it. 3) Implement the weenie seam: IS_PLAYER movers only; bypass when the player has IgnoreHouseBarriers. Resolve the restriction object from WorldState entities; a missing object is Collided. Allow when house_owner == mover, else evaluate HouseRestrictionsData (open house / allegiance / guest list, same as OpenAC IsAllowedIn and ACE House.CanMoveInto). 4) Port CLandCell::handle_move_restriction's axis-aligned collision normal for the outdoor case. Escape `?houseBarriers=off`.
test_plan: holtburger-world: a fixture cell with restriction_obj = a house entity. A non-guest player's step is Collided; the owner, a guest (restriction list) and an IgnoreHouseBarriers player pass; a missing restriction object is Collided; non-player movers are unaffected. Parse test: LandBlockInfo RestrictionTables -> outdoor cell ids via gid_to_lcoord, as in ACE Landblock.cs:508-519. Live: walk into a locked villa yard in a housing area.

title: The heightfield fallback (used while terrain streams in, and under ?faithfulOutdoor=off) inverts retail water: every all-water CELL is a wall, codes 22/23 count as water, and the floor is RAISED by the wading depth instead of sunk
decomp_evidence: TERRAIN_SURF_CHAR (acclient.c:41303) marks only codes 16-20 WATER (21-31 SOLID). OBJECTINFO::validate_walkable (:314223-314227) computes `v17 = N·(c − r·ẑ) + d + water_depth`, so the sphere rests water_depth BELOW the terrain plane (0.45/0.1 partially water via calc_water_depth :353646, 0.9 entirely water via get_water_depth :347233). Only a fully-flooded LANDBLOCK is a wall (finding landdefs-terrain-1).
openac_evidence: TerrainSurface.cs per-vertex water mask `typeBits >= 0x10 && typeBits <= 0x14`; OpenSeaBarrierTests.Player_CanWadeWhereTheBlockIsOnlyPartlyWater (an all-water cell in a partly-water block is walkable).
holt_evidence: crates/holtburger-world/src/state/types.rs:34-36 `matches!(code & 0x1f, 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 22 | 23)`. types.rs is_entirely_water_cell_at is documented as making 'the cell a hard wall for walkers'; it is used at spatial/transition.rs:1442 and movement/system.rs:6837. transition.rs:1263 and system.rs:6781 use `z + env.water_depth_at(...)`, a raised floor ('wades ON the raised plane'). The faithful path does it right: faithful_bridge.rs classify_cell_water uses 16..=20, and the objectinfo.rs:81 validate_walkable port adds water_depth to the signed distance (it sinks). The faithful_bridge.rs:1100 comment already flags the 22/23 mismatch.
discrepancy: Whenever the faithful driver delegates to the heightfield path (the begin LB's terrain is not yet resident in SpatialScene, e.g. right after a teleport or while running into a fresh LB, or with faithfulOutdoor=off), a player in water floats 0.45-0.9 m above the surface instead of sinking. Lake cells are walls, and FauxWater (22/23) shores behave as water. When the scene catches up, the faithful path snaps the player down by up to 1.8 m.
proposed_change: Make the fallback match retail and the faithful path: (a) is_water_terrain_code -> 16..=20 only; (b) use `z - water_depth_at(...)` (the resting floor sits depth below the plane) at transition.rs:1263/1384/1579 and system.rs:189/6781; (c) replace the per-cell `is_entirely_water_cell_at` wall with a per-landblock all-water test, plus the viewer/missile exemptions, sharing the helper from landdefs-terrain-1. Behind the existing USE_WATER_COLLISION carrier, or a new `?legacyWaterRetail` default-on escape.
test_plan: holtburger-world state tests: code 22/23 vertices are not water; water_depth on a shoreline cell lowers the resolved floor by 0.45/0.1; an all-water cell in a partly-water LB is walkable at -0.9; an all-water LB refuses the step. Re-pin any existing F4-4 tests that encode the raised floor. Live: enter a lake right after a teleport (fallback window) and confirm there is no float-then-drop.
already_tracked: Partly: the faithful_bridge.rs:1100 NOTE flags the 22/23 codes only

title: Book page permissions are not modelled: Edit/Save/Delete are offered on every page (quest/library books included) because the snapshot drops author_id and ignore_author, and ACE acks every modify with success=true, so a refused edit silently reverts
decomp_evidence: gmBookUI::DisplayPageData (acclient.c:238214): `if ( v2->authorID == v6 || v2->ignoreAuthor ) SetEditable(m_pageText, 1); else { Deselect; SetEditable(m_pageText, 0); }` with v6 = SmartBox player_id. gmBookUI::CloseCurPage (:238301) only sends Event_BookModifyPage/Event_BookDeletePage for a page that is `authorID == player || ignoreAuthor`, and deletes only a blank page the player authored. gmBookUI::OpenBook (:238737) titles the book with the inscription when `scribeID` is set, else the object name.
openac_evidence: RuntimeBookState.IsEditableLocked: `page.IgnoreAuthor != 0u || page.AuthorId == playerGuid`. FlushCurrentPageLocked returns None for a non-editable page. IRuntimeBookView.IsPageEditable gates the UI. BookMessages.ReadPage keeps AuthorId / IgnoreAuthor / TextIncluded per page.
holt_evidence: src/lib.rs:31036-31039 `struct BookPageView { author_name, text }`; publish_player_book_snapshot (src/lib.rs:44519-44545) maps only author_name + page_text. holtburger-world book.rs BookPage has author_id / ignore_author / text_included, but they never reach JS. plugins/book-panel.js:374 `refs.editBtn.disabled = reading && total === 0;` and :382 `refs.delBtn.disabled = total <= 0;` are the only gates. :432 `// ignore_author=false; ACE ignores this field`. :316 title is always objectDisplayName. ACE: Player_Book.cs HandleActionBookModifyPage sends `GameEventBookModifyPageResponse(..., true)` whatever Book.ModifyPage returned (the permission check is in Book.cs ModifyPage/DeletePage).
discrepancy: A player can 'edit' a read-only book: type, press Save, see the panel re-fetch, and the text silently snaps back. Delete on a page they didn't write fails the same way. Retail never lets them type into such a page.
proposed_change: Carry `authorId`, `ignoreAuthor`, `textIncluded` (and the book-level scribe id) through BookPageView/BookPageViewJs and BookSnapshotJs. In book-panel.js compute `editable = page.ignoreAuthor || page.authorId === localPlayerGuid`. Disable Edit/Delete for non-editable pages (Delete is retail's 'blank your own page'; see books-journal-2). Title the window with the inscription when the scribe id is non-zero, as retail does. No flag needed (UI fix), or `?bookPerms=off`.
test_plan: Node: book-panel unit with a debug snapshot (window.__bookPanelDebug.render) whose pages carry authorId != local guid and ignoreAuthor=false. Edit and Delete should be disabled; with ignoreAuthor=true or authorId == local guid they are enabled. Rust: snapshot projection test that the new fields are copied. Live: open a quest/lore book from an NPC; Edit should be greyed.

title: Book writing loses text and skips retail's page-turn protocol: closing/cancelling while editing discards the typed page (retail CloseCurPage saves it), and add/delete are buttons instead of retail's add-on-turn-past-end / delete-blank-own-page with the requestPending gate
decomp_evidence: gmBookUI::CloseBook (acclient.c:238386) calls CloseCurPage first. CloseCurPage (:238301) sends Event_BookModifyPage with the page text, or Event_BookDeletePage + local PageDataList::Delete when the player's own page is blank (PageTextBlank). gmBookUI::SetCurPage (:238407) runs CloseCurPage on every turn and shifts the target index after a delete. A target past the last page sends Event_BookAddPage, a page without text sends Event_BookPageData, and both set requestPending, which refuses further turns. Turning past a blank last page you wrote is refused with `"The %s is already open to a blank page"` (ECM_UI DisplayStringInfo 0x1A). BookAddPageResponseEvent (:238532) inserts the new page locally and re-requests the whole book (Event_BookData) only on failure or an index mismatch.
openac_evidence: RuntimeBookState.TurnPageLocked/FlushCurrentPageLocked implement the same flow: the RefusedLastPageBlank, DeletePage/ModifyPage flush, AddPage and RequestPageText actions, and the _requestPending gate. ApplyAddPageResponse inserts a blank player-authored page. OpenAC also flushes on close: src/AcDream.App/UI/Layout/BookPanelController.cs:235-251 OnHidden ('Closing a book saves the open page first, the same as turning away from it') calls FlushCurrentPage and then CloseBook.
holt_evidence: plugins/book-panel.js:181 `onHide: () => { mode = "read"; }` and the onEscape/Cancel handlers drop the textarea contents. Saving happens only on the explicit Save (onSavePage :421). Add/Delete are buttons (bookAddPage / bookDeletePage). Every write is followed by a blind `refetch` (:398, setTimeout 200 ms → bookData). Pages are never fetched with bookPageData (no export; 0x00AE is unused). No requestPending gate.
discrepancy: Text typed and then closed (X, Esc twice, or walking off and closing) is lost, where retail saves it. There is no refusal message for appending after a blank page. Every action costs an extra full BookData round trip.
proposed_change: Port the gmBookUI flow into book-panel.js, keyed on books-journal-1's editability: (1) flush on close/hide and on page turn: if editable, blank and own → bookDeletePage, else if changed → bookModifyPage. (2) Next on the last page, when below maxNumPages, sends bookAddPage, with a pending gate until kind:24 arrives, and is refused with the retail line when the last page is your own blank page. (3) Drop the blind 200 ms refetch: fold Add/Delete/Modify responses as retail does and re-request BookData only on failure. Keep the explicit buttons as an optional dev affordance only if the owner wants them (UI policy: retail).
test_plan: Node: a book-panel state test with a fake handle recording calls: type, then close, and the call is bookModifyPage(page, text); blank your own page, then turn, and it is bookDeletePage and the index shifts; Next on the last page calls bookAddPage once and a second Next while pending is a no-op; blank own last page, then Next, gives the refusal text and no call.

title: Inscriptions are written from the book panel for any book, with an optimistic 'Inscription saved', while the examine panel is read-only. Retail inscribes from the examine panel, only on Inscribable items not signed by someone else
decomp_evidence: ItemExamineUI::SetInscription (acclient.c:229275-229380): the inscription box is shown only when the item is Inscribable (PublicWeenieDesc bitfield bit 1, or AppraisalProfile::IsHookedItemInscribable). With no ScribeName (string 8) it shows `<Inscribe here>`; otherwise the inscription (string 7) plus `--ScribeName` (account appended for PSRs). The save path (:229410-229449) sends CM_Writing::Event_SetInscription only when the text differs from m_old_inscription.
openac_evidence: OpenAC parses the stand-alone inscription answer but notes 'Retail's own client has no handler for it' (BookMessages.cs ParseInscription). Book inscriptions are display-only in RuntimeBookState (ApplyInscription retitles).
holt_evidence: plugins/book-panel.js:231 an Inscribe button on every book. onSaveInscription (:402-418) calls setInscription and toasts 'Inscription saved' (:415) without waiting for anything. plugins/examine-target.js renderInscription is read-only ('P2-44: examine never prompts for an inscription'). ACE refuses non-Inscribable items and items scribed by another character without telling the client (Player_Inventory.cs:3650-3664).
discrepancy: Players are offered inscription on books that can't take one, or that someone else signed, and are told it worked. Inscribable weapons, armour and gems (the common retail case) have no inscribe UI except a slash command.
proposed_change: Move writing to the examine panel per retail. Make the inscription area editable when the appraised item is Inscribable and either has no ScribeName (placeholder `<Inscribe here>`) or the ScribeName is the local character. Send setInscription on blur/close only when the text changed. Drop the book-panel Inscribe button, or apply the same gate and remove the optimistic toast.
test_plan: Node (test_examine_format.mjs style): an appraisal with Inscribable and no ScribeName renders an editable box with the placeholder; ScribeName = another player renders read-only text with the '--Name' signature; a non-inscribable item shows no box; a changed text on close calls setInscription once.
already_tracked: P2-44 chose read-only examine; not in the comparison ledgers

title: A book that is not in the player's inventory (shelf/hook) is never closed when the player walks out of its use range
decomp_evidence: gmBookUI::OpenBook (acclient.c:238737): `if ( !ACCWeenieObject::IsOwnedByPlayer(...) ) CPlayerSystem::RegisterObjectRangeHandler(..., bookID, _range /* object's use radius */, ...)`. gmBookUI::OnObjectRangeExit (:237788) closes the book panel for that object.
openac_evidence: RuntimeBookState.CloseBook closes when the panel hides or the session ends; OpenAC has no range close either (retail is the reference here).
holt_evidence: plugins/book-panel.js has no distance or range handling. The panel stays open until closed by hand. ACE's book actions resolve the book through SearchLocations.LastUsedHook (Player_Book.cs), so edits keep working from any distance.
discrepancy: Reading or writing a housing-hook / library book keeps working after walking away. Retail closes the book at the edge of use range.
proposed_change: When the opened book's guid is not in the player's inventory, watch distance on the existing per-frame/HUD tick (the trade range watcher from round-2 trade-2 is the pattern). Past the object's use radius (UseRadius, or a ~3 m default), run the books-journal-2 flush and close the panel. Flag `?bookRangeClose` (default on).
test_plan: Node: with a stubbed entity position and player pose, moving past the radius closes the panel and flushes; an inventory book never closes on distance.

title: Server confirmation requests (GameEvent 0x0274) have no player UI: the craft success-chance dialog is never shown, so tinkering/imbuing does nothing with the dialog option on. Fellowship invites, allegiance swears, aug/skill/attribute devices and yes/no emotes are unanswerable too
decomp_evidence: ClientUISystem::Handle_Character__ConfirmationRequest (acclient.c:401345) dispatches by type: 1 SwearAllegiance, 2 AlterSkill, 3 AlterAttribute, 4 Fellowship, 5 CraftInteraction, 6 Augmentation, 7 YesNo. Each goes to a UI notice. gmGamePlayUI::RecvNotice_CraftInteraction_ConfirmationRequest (:280763) appends " Continue?" to the server text and calls MakeGameplayConfirmationDialog, whose answer is CM_Character::Event_ConfirmationResponse. ConfirmationDone/AbortConfirmationRequest close the dialog (gmGamePlayUI/gmFellowshipUI/gmAllegianceUI::RecvNotice_AbortConfirmationRequest).
openac_evidence: Not in the listed OpenAC crafting files. OpenAC's item path only sends UseWithTarget (RuntimeItemInteraction SendUseWithTarget); the retail dispatch above is the reference.
holt_evidence: apps/holtburger-web/src/session/messages/game_event.rs:116-127 pushes CharacterConfirmationRequest into `pending_confirmations` ('Deliberately NOT a chat line'). The wasm exports pendingConfirmations / sendConfirmationResponse (src/lib.rs:40791, :40804), but the only JS caller is the bot host (rynth/webhost.js:154, :1189; rynth/ai/confirm_reflex.js auto-yes). plugins/, app/ and index.html never read them. CharacterConfirmationDone (0x0276) has no arm. Running ACE (~/ace-server/Source/ACE.Server/Managers/RecipeManager.cs:94): `showDialog = HasDifficulty(recipe) && player.GetCharacterOption(CharacterOption.UseCraftingChanceOfSuccessDialog)`. ShowDialog (:322-345) sends 'You determine that you have a N percent chance to succeed.' (+ augmentation line) through ConfirmationManager, which aborts after 30 s (ConfirmationManager.cs:20). ACE also routes Fellowship.cs:126 invites, Player_Allegiance.cs:90 swears, AugmentationDevice/SkillAlterationDevice/AttributeTransferDevice, Gem.cs:79 and EmoteManager.cs:832 yes/no through the same request.
discrepancy: With the (retail-common) crafting-chance option on, every tinker, imbue or other difficulty recipe plays the clap animation and then silently does nothing; the player never sees the chance. The player also cannot accept a fellowship invite or a vassal's swear, use aug gems or skill/attribute alteration devices, or answer quest yes/no prompts.
proposed_change: 1) wasm: emit a client event on 0x0274 (type, context, text) and on 0x0276 ConfirmationDone (type, context), keeping the pending queue for the bot. 2) A plugin (e.g. plugins/server-confirm.js) opens modal-dialog.js per request with retail text per type: CraftInteraction = text + ' Continue?'; YesNo/Augmentation/AlterSkill/AlterAttribute = the server text; Fellowship and SwearAllegiance with the requester name from text. Yes/No calls sendConfirmationResponse(type, context, accepted). ConfirmationDone for the same (type, context) closes the dialog without sending. 3) A second request of the same type replaces the first, as retail's single dialog slot does. No flag (missing feature); `?serverConfirm=off` escape if wanted.
test_plan: Node: a server-confirm plugin unit with a fake handle: a CraftInteraction request shows '<text> Continue?'; Yes sends (5, ctx, true); No sends false; ConfirmationDone closes without sending. Rust: the recv arm emits the client event and still queues. Live: with UseCraftingChanceOfSuccessDialog on, apply salvage to an item, accept, and the recipe runs; invite a second character to a fellowship and accept.

title: The salvage window accepts items retail refuses: no gmSalvageUI::IsItemSuitable gate (valid material, structure < 100, not Retained, single-material lock when 'Salvage multiple materials' is off), and pack contents go in unfiltered
decomp_evidence: gmSalvageUI::IsItemSuitable (acclient.c:252433) requires `TinkeringSystem::IsValidMaterialType(material) && pwd._structure < 0x64 && (PlayerModule::SalvageMultiple || m_material == 0 || material == m_material)` and then `~BYTE3(pwd._bitfield) & 1` (not Retained, 0x01000000). IsValidMaterialType (:500471): materials 1,2,4-8,10-55,57-64,66-71,73-77. gmSalvageUI::_AddItem (:252614) runs the gate and locks m_material to the first item. _AddContainedItems (:252758) prints 'Adding contents of %s' and runs _AddItem on each contained item, recursing. DragItemAcceptable (:252825) checks ownership ('You can only salvage items that you own!').
openac_evidence: src/AcDream.Core/Items/SalvageItemPolicy.cs IsValidMaterial (the same set) plus IsSuitable(material, Structure < 100, bitfield, allowMultipleMaterials). RuntimeItemInteraction.TrySalvageItems refuses the whole send when any item is unsuitable. (OpenAC masks the bitfield with 0xFF000000, broader than retail's single Retained bit.)
holt_evidence: plugins/salvage-panel.js addFromDrop (:297-325) checks only tool presence, ownership, equipped and container. Containers add their direct children with no suitability check. addItem (:288-294) dedupes only. inventoryRows (commerce_window.js:362-379) carries no material, structure or bitfield, so the gate cannot be computed in JS today. ACE silently skips Retained and no-workmanship items (~/ace-server ... Player_Crafting.cs HandleSalvaging: `if (item.Workmanship == null || item.Retained) continue;`) and does not enforce the single-material option.
discrepancy: Players can queue Retained items (skipped by the server with no message), full 100-unit bags and unsalvageable materials. With the multiple-materials option off, mixed materials are salvaged anyway, so the guard players rely on against destroying the wrong items does nothing.
proposed_change: Add a wasm/world helper `salvageSuitable(guid, lockedMaterial)`, a port of IsItemSuitable reading the entity's MaterialType, Structure and PWD bitfield (holtburger-common ObjectDescriptionFlag RETAINED = 0x01000000) and the player's SalvageMultiple option. Use it in addFromDrop and when expanding a pack (recursive, with the retail 'Adding contents of %s' line). Lock to the first item's material when the option is off. Precondition: fix the round-2-noted character_option_mask bug in holtburger-world player/types.rs, which maps AllowOthersToSeeYourAge to SALVAGE_MULTIPLE, so the option reads correctly.
test_plan: Rust: the IsItemSuitable port is true for material 0x0B (Amber) structure 50; false for material 0x09 (Gem), structure 100, the Retained bit, and a second material with SalvageMultiple off. Node: salvage-panel addFromDrop with a stubbed helper rejects unsuitable items and filters pack contents. Live: try to add a Retained item and a full bag.
already_tracked: Partly: round-2 §6 notes the SALVAGE_MULTIPLE bit-mapping bug

title: Salvage results never reach chat: retail prints 'You obtain N Material (ws X.XX), … using your knowledge of Salvaging.' plus the augmentation bonus; holtburger only logs to the console and adds a differently-worded row while the salvage window is open
decomp_evidence: ClientUISystem::Handle_Inventory__Recv_SalvageOperationsResultData (acclient.c:402586) builds the list with GenerateMaterialsSalvagedString (:402430, `"%s%d %s (ws %.2lf)"` joined), adds `" Your augmentation has given you a return bonus of %d%%!"` when GetAugBonus is non-zero, formats `L"You obtain %hs using your knowledge of %hs.%s\n"` with AppraisalSystem::SkillToString(skill), and calls AddTextToScroll. A non-empty not-salvageable list adds `" The following were not suitable for salvaging: …"` (GenerateNonSuitablesString).
openac_evidence: None in the listed files (retail is the reference).
holt_evidence: app/client_events.js:1245-1265 (SalvageOperationsResult kind) decodes skill/augBonus/results, `console.log`s them and emits `salvageResult`. plugins/salvage-panel.js appendResult (:333-343) renders `You obtain ${units} × ${material} (workmanship x.xx)` only while the panel is open. augBonus and skill are dropped. A search for 'using your knowledge' finds nothing.
discrepancy: Players who close the window or salvage via the bot path get no record of what they obtained, and the wording, skill name and augmentation note differ from retail.
proposed_change: In client_events.js on kind 52, build the retail line: materials as `${n} ${MaterialName} (ws ${w.toFixed(2)})` joined by ', '; skill name via handle.skillName(skill); the aug clause when augBonus > 0. Append it to chat (the server already applies the Salvaging squelch). Have the panel's Results rows reuse the same per-material text. Handle a non-zero not_salvagable list with the retail 'The following were not suitable…' line (ACE sends 0 today).
test_plan: Node: a pure formatter test. results [{material: 0x3D (Iron), units: 12, workmanship: 5.4166}], skill = Salvaging, augBonus 25 gives 'You obtain 12 Iron (ws 5.42) using your knowledge of Salvaging. Your augmentation has given you a return bonus of 25%!'. Also: no aug clause when augBonus is 0, and a multi-material join with ', '.
